correctness.rationale: For a nonzero UQNA bounded S:c0(Gamma)->Y, Hahn–Banach yields y* norm 1 at its distinguished image u, and f=y* S∈(c0(Gamma))*=ell1(Gamma) with ||f||=||S||=r by a norming-image subsequence. Any unit-ball sequence with Re f(x_n)->r must satisfy Sx_n->u: otherwise a subsequence away from u has a further UQNA-convergent subsequence to phase theta u, where the f-limit forces theta=1. Exhaust the countable ell1-support of f by finite F_n with tail mass tau_n->0 and choose a_n supported in F_n attaining f(a_n)=r−tau_n. If ||S(I−P_Fn)|| fails to vanish, select norm<=1 z_n outside F_n with ||Sz_n||>=delta. Then a_n±z_n remain in the c0 unit ball, and Re f(a_n±z_n)>=r−2tau_n, so S(a_n±z_n)->u and 2Sz_n->0: contradiction. Thus S is a norm limit of finite-rank SP_Fn and compact, even for uncountable Gamma and arbitrary real/complex Y.
